milestone: Bacterial & archaeal homologous DNA repair and mating bridges
plain_text: Before two-parent sex existed, bacteria and archaea used RecA/RadA enzymes to patch broken DNA from neighbor strands and pass genes across cell-to-cell bridges.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Parasexual horizontal transfer (transformation, viral transduction, archaeal cytoplasmic bridges)
parental_and_social_investment: None — single cells divide on their own
source: Dagan, Artzy-Randrup & Martin (2008) PNAS 105:10039; Naor & Gophna (2013) Trends Microbiol. 21:259
date_source: Moody et al. (2024) Nat. Ecol. Evol. 8:1654; Lawrence & Ochman (1998) PNAS 95:9413
note: Homologous recombination likely evolved first to repair double-strand DNA breaks, then became the engine of later meiosis.

milestone: Core eukaryotic meiotic recombination toolkit (Spo11, Dmc1, Msh4/5)
plain_text: The common ancestor of all complex cells repurposed DNA-repair enzymes to line up two chromosome sets, swap matching segments, and deal one clean half into each gamete.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Syngamy (cell fusion) + two-step meiotic reduction division
parental_and_social_investment: Diploid backup copy masks single recessive mutations
source: Ramesh, Malik & Logsdon (2005) Curr. Biol. 15:185; Speijer, Lukeš & Eliáš (2015) PNAS 112:8827
date_source: Betts et al. (2018) Nat. Ecol. Evol. 2:1556; Miao et al. (2019) Precambrian Res. 321:172
note: Because protists like Giardia and Trichomonas carry meiosis-only genes, true meiotic sex predates the split of living complex cells.

milestone: Isogamy and plus/minus molecular mating types
plain_text: Equal-sized swimming cells evolved surface recognition tags—plus and minus—so stressed cells fuse only with an opposite partner and form a hardy resting spore.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Isogamy: two equal-sized flagellated gametes (mt+ and mt−)
parental_and_social_investment: Uniparental organelle inheritance (only one parent passes chloroplast/mitochondrial DNA, curbing selfish organelle conflict)
source: Ferris & Goodenough (1997) Genetics 146:859; Goodenough & Heitman (2014) Cold Spring Harb. Perspect. Biol. 6:a016154
date_source: Bengtson et al. (2017) PLoS Biol. 15:e2000735; Tang et al. (2020) Nat. Ecol. Evol. 4:543
note: Facultative sex: algae divide clonally in good times and switch to sexual fusion when nitrogen or water runs scarce.

milestone: Oldest fossil sexual reproduction in a multicellular organism
plain_title: First fossil sex in a red seaweed
plain_text: Rocks 1.05 billion years old preserve Bangiomorpha pubescens with distinct four-part spore packets—the unmistakable signature of meiotic sex in a many-celled body.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Differentiated sexual carpogonia and spermatia in multicellular filaments
parental_and_social_investment: Single-cell zygote bottleneck aligns clone cells to build holdfast and upright frond
date_source: Gibson et al. (2018) Geology 46:135 (Re-Os date: 1,047 +13/-17 Ma)
note: Marks the transition where sex stops being an emergency microbial backup and becomes woven into building multicellular bodies.

milestone: Anisogamy — divergence into tiny motile sperm and large nutrient-rich eggs
plain_title: Why gametes split into sperm and egg
plain_text: Growing a bigger body rewards a food-packed egg, while finding a partner rewards millions of tiny fast swimmers. Middle-sized gametes lose out, creating biological males and females.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Oogamy / anisogamy (egg volume 10^4–10^7x larger than flagellated sperm)
parental_and_social_investment: Maternal egg stocks yolk, ribosomes and mRNA to power early cleavage divisions
source: Parker, Baker & Smith (1972) J. Theor. Biol. 36:529; Hanschen et al. (2018) Evolution 72:386
date_source: Herron et al. (2009) PNAS 106:3254; dos Reis et al. (2015) Curr. Biol. 25:2939
note: Evolved convergently in animals, land plants, red/brown algae and volvocine green algae as multicellularity scaled up.

milestone: Lunar-synchronized broadcast spawning & peptide sperm chemotaxis
plain_title: Reef-wide spawning by moonlight and scent
plain_text: Early sea animals coordinate whole populations with light-sensing opsins and temperature to release gametes in the same hour, then guide sperm with species-specific egg scents.
gamete_and_mating_mode: External synchronized broadcast spawning + Ca2+-channel sperm chemotaxis (CatSper)
parental_and_social_investment: Mass synchronization swamps predators; species-specific bindin/egg coat locks prevent hybrid waste
source: Babcock et al. (1986) Mar. Biol. 90:379; Kaupp, Kashikar & Weyand (2008) Annu. Rev. Physiol. 70:93
date_source: Putnam et al. (2007) Science 317:86; Evans et al. (2020) PNAS 117:7845
note: Sperm swim up femtomolar gradients of egg peptides using millisecond calcium spikes.

milestone: Arthropod mate recognition, dimorphic claspers & earliest fossil brood care
plain_title: Compound eyes, claspers and carried eggs
plain_text: Cambrian arthropods use sharp compound eyes and antennae to find individual mates, and fossil Waptia shrimps already carry protective clusters of up to 24 eggs under their shells.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Targeted arthropod pairing + maternal carapace egg brooding
parental_and_social_investment: Direct maternal ventilation and protection of small clutch (~24 eggs)
source: Caron & Vannier (2016) Curr. Biol. 26:69; Duan et al. (2014) Geology 42:499
date_source: Caron & Vannier (2016) Curr. Biol. 26:69 (Burgess Shale, ~508 Ma)
note: Shows the classic r/K trade-off appearing right in the Cambrian: fewer, larger eggs kept safe by a parent.

milestone: Earliest vertebrate copulation and internal fertilization
plain_text: Fossil placoderms preserve bony male claspers and female pelvic plates—replacing open-water gamete clouds with direct side-by-side internal fertilization.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Paired pelvic claspers + internal fertilization (and live birth with umbilical cord in Materpiscis)
parental_and_social_investment: Individual mate choice + protected internal embryo development (~380 Ma Materpiscis fossil embryo)
source: Long et al. (2015) Nature 517:196; Long et al. (2008) Nature 453:650
date_source: Long et al. (2015) Nature 517:196 (Middle Devonian Givetian, ~385 Ma)
note: Remarkably, many later ray-finned bony fishes reverted to external spawning before tetrapods re-evolved internal mating on land.

milestone: Seed-plant pollen tubes and waterproof amniote land reproduction
plain_title: Sex cuts its last tie to open water
plain_text: Seed plants grow microscopic pollen tubes directly to the ovule while land reptiles pair internally to lay shelled amniotic eggs with their own private pond.
representative_organism: Hylonomus lyelli (early amniote) & Carboniferous seed plants
gamete_and_mating_mode: Airborne/insect-borne pollen tubes (plants); internal copulation + shelled cleidoic egg (amniotes)
parental_and_social_investment: Large yolk + amnion, chorion and allantois membranes sustain weeks of air-breathing embryonic growth
source: Carroll (1964) J. Linn. Soc. Lond. Zool. 45:61; Linkies et al. (2010) New Phytol. 186:817
date_source: Benton et al. (2015) Palaeontology 58:1 (Joggins Formation Hylonomus, ~315 Ma)
note: Both kingdoms independently solved terrestrial desiccation within the same Carboniferous interval.

milestone: Dedicated XY and ZW genetic sex chromosomes
plain_title: Chromosomes take over from nest warmth
plain_text: Ancestors of placental/marsupial mammals and birds independently locked sex determination onto XY and ZW chromosome pairs, guaranteeing balanced 50:50 sex ratios across climates.
representative_organism: Therian mammal ancestor (SRY / XY) & avian ancestor (DMRT1 / ZW)
gamete_and_mating_mode: Heteromorphic chromosomal sex determination (XY male heterogamety; ZW female heterogamety)
parental_and_social_investment: Protects warm-blooded lineages against climate-skewed single-sex broods
source: Veyrunes et al. (2008) Genome Res. 18:965; Cortez et al. (2014) Nature 508:488
date_source: Cortez et al. (2014) Nature 508:488 (~166–180 Ma origin of therian SRY)
note: Egg-laying monotremes (platypus) carry a separate 10-sex-chromosome chain, proving mammal XY arose after therians split.

plain_text: Flowering plants trade color, scent and nectar so insects and birds carry pollen miles to distant mates, backed by genetic locks that reject self-pollen and double fertilization.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Animal-vectored cross-pollination + S-locus self-incompatibility + double fertilization (3n endosperm)
parental_and_social_investment: Plants invest endosperm food ONLY after fertilization succeeds, slashing wasted seed cost
source: Amborella Genome Project (2013) Science 342:1241089; Bao et al. (2019) PNAS 116:24707
date_source: Hughes (1994) The Enigma of Angiosperm Origins (~130 Ma Barremian tricolpate/early pollen); Bao et al. (2019) (~99 Ma Burmese amber beetle pollination)
note: Co-drove insect color vision, olfactory mushroom-body memory (honeybees remember floral refill schedules) and terrestrial productivity.

milestone: Haplodiploid sex determination, nuptial flights & queen sperm banks
plain_title: One nuptial flight fuels a million-worker colony
plain_text: In ants, bees and wasps, fertilized eggs grow into females and unfertilized eggs into males; a young queen mates on one flight and stores live sperm for up to 20 years.
representative_organism: Atta leafcutter ants & Apis mellifera honeybees
gamete_and_mating_mode: Haplodiploidy + polyandrous nuptial flight + multi-decade spermatheca storage
parental_and_social_investment: Thousands to millions of sterile sisters rear brood collectively (superorganism germline/soma split)
source: Hamilton (1964) J. Theor. Biol. 7:1; Baer (2005) Trends Ecol. Evol. 20:670; Hölldobler & Wilson (2009)
date_source: Grimaldi & Agosti (2000) PNAS 97:13678; Perrichot et al. (2008) Proc. R. Soc. B (~100 Ma Cretaceous ants)
note: Multiple mating by queens increases genetic diversity inside the hive, improving disease resistance and task division.

stage: 6. Placental care, neural courtship & human family bonds
milestone: Placental gestation, genomic imprinting & oxytocin maternal bonding
plain_text: Placental mammals nourish embryos internally for months while parent-specific epigenetic tags balance fetal growth, followed by oxytocin-bonded nursing and teaching.
gamete_and_mating_mode: Internal fertilization + invasive chorioallantoic placenta + parent-of-origin genomic imprinting
parental_and_social_investment: Months of bloodstream provisioning + lactation + juvenile play and social learning
source: Haig (1993) Q. Rev. Biol. 68:495; Broad, Curley & Keverne (2006) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 361:2199
date_source: O'Leary et al. (2013) Science 339:662; Halliday, Upchurch & Goswami (2017) Biol. Rev. 92:521
note: Viral syncytin genes captured from ancient retroviruses were co-opted to fuse placental membranes!

stage: 6. Placental care, neural courtship & human family bonds
milestone: Cognitive mate choice, learned courtship song & aesthetic displays
plain_title: Songs, dances and brains shaped by mate choice
plain_text: Songbirds, bowerbirds and whales turn courtship into cognitive theater—learning hundreds of phrases, mimicking rivals or building symmetrical stages judged by discerning mates.
representative_organism: Oscine songbirds (Menura lyrebird), bowerbirds & humpback whales
gamete_and_mating_mode: Culturally transmitted acoustic/visual courtship + female cognitive mate assessment
parental_and_social_investment: Biparental nest provisioning (90% of bird species) + socially learned vocal traditions
source: Darwin (1871); Prum (2017) The Evolution of Beauty; Jarvis (2019) Science 366:50; Garland et al. (2011) Curr. Biol. 21:687
date_source: Oliveros et al. (2019) PNAS 116:7916 (~33–47 Ma crown oscine songbird radiation)
note: Sexual selection turns nervous systems themselves into evolutionary evaluators, accelerating sensory and vocal-learning circuits.

stage: 6. Placental care, neural courtship & human family bonds
milestone: Human pair bonding, concealed ovulation & three-generation grandmother care
plain_text: Humans combine concealed ovulation, lasting pair bonds, non-conceptive socio-sexual bonding and post-menopausal grandmothers—pooling calories and teaching across three generations.
representative_organism: Homo sapiens & Middle Pleistocene hominins (plus Pan paniscus socio-sexual comparison)
gamete_and_mating_mode: Multi-family residential bands + enduring pair bonds + concealed ovulation + ~70 de novo mutations/birth
parental_and_social_investment: ~13 million kilocalories and 15–18 years of biparental, sibling and grandmother provisioning per child
source: Hawkes et al. (1998) PNAS 95:1336; Hrdy (2009) Mothers and Others; Kaplan et al. (2000) Evol. Anthropol. 9:156
date_source: Hublin et al. (2017) Nature 546:289; Smith et al. (2010) PNAS 107:20923 (prolonged dental/life-history maturation)
note: Only humans and a few toothed whales (orcas, pilot whales, narwhals) evolved long post-reproductive female lifespans that boost grandchildren's survival.

stage: 6. Placental care, neural courtship & human family bonds
milestone: Assisted reproduction (IVF), cryopreservation, embryo genome screening & lab gametogenesis
plain_title: IVF, frozen gametes and reading embryo genomes
plain_text: Contraception decouples sex from reproduction while IVF, liquid-nitrogen banking, genetic embryo screening and lab-grown mouse eggs bring conscious information tools into conception.
representative_organism: Clinical human IVF / PGT-M & mouse in-vitro gametogenesis
gamete_and_mating_mode: Ex-vivo fertilization (IVF/ICSI) + vitrification at -196 °C + single-cell embryo sequencing
parental_and_social_investment: Over 12 million IVF births since 1978 + global public schooling and digital knowledge inheritance
source: Steptoe & Edwards (1978) Lancet 312:366; Handyside et al. (1990) Nature 344:768; Hayashi et al. (2016) Nature 539:299
date_source: Steptoe & Edwards (1978) first IVF birth; PGT whole-genome embryo screening & iPSC gametogenesis (2012–2026)
note: Marks the first time in 4 billion years that a lineage inspects and freezes its own gametes and embryonic genomes before development.
